title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Locomotion 024 — Pole Plant / Third Support / Runout

source.identity: Donatello — Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Tournament Fighters — SNES — Fighters
observed: The commissioned evidence explicitly treated the entire 568×2297 static sheet as one source corpus.
A long-weapon fighter sheet visibly includes travel/jump, staff-extension, action, and consequence/recovery families.
The static sheet supplies no trustworthy source-authentic exposure duration, root trajectory, support transfer, or chronological ordering.
unknown: Source-authentic chronology/exposure, root coordinates, exact support transfer, pole-plant locomotion choreography, force magnitudes, and gameplay cadence are unknown.

rights.output_description: independent generic ASCII biped/root-support rig using an abstract pole as a temporary third support anchor

novelty.new_causality: A carried pole becomes a temporary third support anchor during locomotion. The pole tip is planted ahead while the rear foot still owns the body; root/COM then pass around the fixed pole tip, a new foot catch must become trustworthy before pole release, and release preserves forward velocity into an overlong free catch followed by shorter corrections and delayed tool/torso settle.
failure_if: pole tip drifts while declared planted
pole contact appears only as metadata
root stops instead of passing the planted anchor
pole releases before a trustworthy foot catch
first free catch is not visibly overlong
tool/torso lag snaps home or ends at idle

timing.playback_policy: authored decisive causal keys with explicit holds; topology-changing support events are authored keys; no reverse interpolation

rig.support_rule: The pole tip is a real world-fixed support only in declared PLANTED_FIXED/UNLOADING_FIXED states. A foot catch must become trustworthy before pole release.
rig.anchor_rule: K02-K07 pole tip remains exactly world-fixed at (250,290). The body/root passes around that anchor; the anchor never follows the root.
rig.release_rule: K08 removes pole support only after K06/K07 establish right-foot ownership. K09 is the largest post-release root-spacing event; K10-K14 shorten and settle displaced.
rig.secondary_rule: Pole/arm lag rises through the pivot/release, peaks after the free overrun, then decays through braking/counterstep/correction without snapping to the approach pose.

keys.name: APPROACH_LEFT_SUPPORT
keys.causal_role: establish asymmetric forward travel and visible pole carriage before any third-support claim

keys.name: POLE_PROBE_AHEAD
keys.causal_role: pole tip reaches fixed ground ahead while the old left support still owns the body; probe is not yet load bearing

keys.name: POLE_PLANT_ACQUIRED
keys.causal_role: commit the pole tip as a real fixed third-support anchor before COM crosses toward it

keys.name: TRIPOD_LOAD_COM_FORWARD
keys.causal_role: compress and drive COM forward through the left-foot plus fixed-pole support triangle while root travel stays live

keys.name: ROOT_PASSES_INTO_POLE_ARC
keys.causal_role: carry root toward the planted pole while unloading the rear foot; pole angle closes around an unchanged world anchor

keys.name: POLE_DOMINANT_SWING_THROUGH
keys.causal_role: let the fixed pole temporarily dominate support while both feet migrate forward; the body passes the anchor instead of teleporting it

keys.name: RIGHT_CATCH_BEFORE_RELEASE
keys.causal_role: earn a trustworthy right-foot catch while the pole tip is still fixed; this catch is the release prerequisite

keys.name: RIGHT_LOAD_POLE_UNLOAD
keys.causal_role: load the new right support and unload the pole without clamping forward velocity; tool lag grows as the body exits its pivot

keys.name: POLE_RELEASE_AFTER_FOOT_OWNERSHIP
keys.causal_role: release the pole tip only after right-foot ownership is established; root velocity survives and the freed pole trails

keys.name: LEFT_FREE_CATCH_OVERRUN
keys.causal_role: first free catch lands deliberately overlong after pole release while the torso and pole remain late

keys.name: LEFT_BRAKE_COMPRESSION
keys.causal_role: hold the overrun catch and compress to brake translation; the pole continues its delayed forward sweep

keys.name: RIGHT_COUNTERSTEP_CATCH
keys.causal_role: short counterstep changes support ownership to catch remaining translational mismatch without becoming a gait loop

keys.name: RIGHT_PASS_LEFT_CORRECTION_PROBE
keys.causal_role: a shorter left correction probe advances while right support remains fixed; secondary tool lag continues to decay

keys.name: LEFT_CORRECTION_CATCH
keys.causal_role: final trusted left correction is smaller than the counterstep and arrests root debt without returning to the original stance

keys.name: DISPLACED_TOOL_LAG_SETTLE
keys.causal_role: settle displaced with left support unloading, residual pole/arm lag, and live next-step debt rather than idle reset

motion_dungeon.compile_chain: AUTHORED ASCII KEYS + DIRECTION PROFILE -> DETERMINISTIC KEY HOLDS -> ASCII-ONLY FRAME RENDER -> H.264 MP4 -> SPA

quality_history.verdict: Pole tip is visibly world-fixed through K02-K07 while root/COM pass around it; right-foot ownership is earned before pole release; K09 is a distinct overlong free catch; K10-K14 visibly shorten and retain delayed tool/torso debt. No support teleport, straight endpoint tween, gait substitution, reverse recovery, or idle reset survives.

The fixed-pole pivot, body crossing the anchor, release fork, long free catch, compressed brake and shrinking correction silhouette sequence is specific, causal and economical without placeholder cheapness.
